summary: XCOM is a full-mesh network architecture for synchronizing multiple QICK boards and their absolute time counters to within 100 ps while providing deterministic all-to-all data communication with latency below 186 ns at 100 MHz clock speed (reducible to 62 ns at 300 MHz). The system combines PLL nested zero-delay mode locking, multi-tile DAC/ADC synchronization, and LVDS-based point-to-point communication via a central fanout hub to enable scalable multi-board control for superconducting and spin qubit systems.
motivation: Superconducting and spin qubit testbeds require expansion beyond single FPGA boards to handle the high I/O count and complex control signals, necessitating precise synchronization and low-latency communication across multiple hardware components without drift or loss of lock.
method: XCOM implements a full-mesh topology with one dedicated $200$ Mb/s LVDS data/clock pair per board (32-bit words at $\sim$100 MHz) transmitted to a central fanout hub using TI DS90LV804 drivers and LMK1D2108 buffers, combined with firmware protocols for network ID auto-assignment, clock reset/start commands, and deterministic message exchange managed by the tProc at the fabric clock (430 MHz).
result: Three RF waveforms from different boards show 20 ps timing skew (demonstrating sub-100 ps cross-board synchronization), 186 ns latency per 32-bit word at current clock speed with drift-free lock stability over multiple days, and the prototype currently supports up to five boards with firmware already supporting 15 boards.
